macro.regime: late-cycle hawkish hold (hike-biased dots), war premium gone, semis rebound on Micron, breadth broadening, hot core PCE
macro.narrative: The hawkish-Fed/no-war regime persists, but the equity tape healed and broadened into late June. (1) The June 16-17 FOMC, Chair Warsh's first, held the funds rate at 3.50-3.75% but the projections leaned hawkish: nine of eighteen members now pencil in at least one hike by year-end (Warsh notably submitted no dot of his own), and the committee withheld forward guidance. A June 25/26 core-PCE print at 3.4% y/y (headline 4.1%, the hottest since 2023) and a BofA call for a series of hikes have pushed market-implied September hike odds up toward ~50-68%. (2) The June 15 US-Iran framework MoU (60-day ceasefire, Strait of Hormuz reopened, naval blockade lifted, Iran oil-sales license) and a June 21-22 roadmap to a final deal are holding but fragile (Lebanon clashes, periodic Hormuz threats). That kept the war premium out: WTI fell below $70 and Brent below $74 (lowest since February, ~40% off the wartime peak), a forward-disinflationary offset to sticky core. (3) The June 23 Asian-led semiconductor rout did NOT extend — Micron's blowout fiscal-Q3 (AI/HBM memory demand) sparked a June 25 rebound (SanDisk +14.7%, Micron +12%), and breadth broadened impressively: the Russell 2000 hit a record 3,000, the small-cap A-D line made an all-time high, and ~62% of the S&P sits above its 200-DMA. Equity-fund flows rotated hard into the US (a record US-equity week, tech +~$21.5B). Rates eased (10y ~4.4%, a 6-week low; 2y ~4.20%; 30y ~4.94%) but the hot PCE and hike-biased dots cap any rally; gold slid to ~$4,040, BTC ~$60-67k and ETH ~$1.6k as crypto sentiment cratered to Extreme Fear (13). NEW this week: China blacklisted MP Materials and USA Rare Earth (June 22), re-igniting the ex-China rare-earth/critical-minerals trade. Net: we hold a modest defensive tilt — OW USD/cash and structurally-bid real assets over richly-valued, concentrated equities (CAPE ~39.7, near-zero ERP) and historically tight credit — but nudge slightly less defensive given the healthier breadth, with the next swings the July 14 June CPI and the July 28-29 FOMC.

drivers.read: S&P CAPE ~39.7 (forward P/E ~23) with a near-zero equity risk premium, top ~10 names ~40% of the index, and IG (~80bp) / HY (~265-285bp) spreads near multi-decade tights leave little cushion for an earnings, capex or growth disappointment — though the June 25 breadth broadening eases the single-stock fragility somewhat.

byAssetClass.note: Solid earnings (Street year-end targets ~8000, DB) and no recession argue up over 12m, and late-June breadth broadened materially (record Russell 2000, ~62% of the S&P above its 200-DMA, Micron-led semis rebound) — easing the single-stock fragility — but a record-low equity risk premium, a ~39.7 CAPE, firm real yields and a hot 3.4% core-PCE keep us Neutral; the next risk events are the July 14 June CPI and the July 28-29 FOMC.

Still the cleanest stagflation hedge — structural central-bank gold demand keeps gold +30%+ y/y at ~$4,040 even after a deeper pullback from its ~$4,724 peak — and the new China rare-earth export curbs (MP/USA Rare Earth blacklisted June 22) add a fresh critical-minerals tailwind; but the call stays only modest OW as WTI has fallen below $70 on the holding US-Iran framework and the rates/USD-driven precious-metals slide adds near-term two-way risk.

BTC is ~$60-67k and ETH ~$1.6k as the hike-biased Fed, hot core PCE and firm dollar offset the US-Iran peace dividend; crypto Fear & Greed cratered to Extreme Fear (13) and spot funds shed ~$6.6B over five weeks (with a tentative late-June stabilization, BTC ETFs +$39M June 23). Higher-for-longer rates keep crypto the highest-beta casualty; 12m odds are genuinely two-sided.

Yields (10y ~4.4% — a 6-week low — 30y ~4.94%) offer attractive carry and a recession hedge, and the oil de-rate lowers forward headline CPI, but a hike-biased Fed and a hot 3.4% core-PCE keep near-term duration risk elevated and us off OW; modest up-bias over 12m as the cycle eventually turns and the energy tail keeps deflating.

The dollar's rate support was reinforced by the hike-biased June FOMC and the hot core-PCE print (September hike odds ~50-68%); cash yields ~3.7-4% with optionality, making USD/cash a high-Sharpe holding while the July 14 June CPI, the July 28-29 FOMC and the durability of the US-Iran roadmap stay unresolved.

calls.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
drivers: 2y yield ~4.16% with very low duration (~1.8y) means carry (~3.4-3.9% annualized) almost entirely drives total return; price volatility is minimal, making this the closest fixed-income analog to cash
Fed hike risk is the dominant headwind — market now pricing a hike by year-end; if materialized, 1-3y yields rise and price dips slightly, but the carry from reinvestment partially offsets within 3m
Positive carry in a high-for-longer regime makes SHY a high-Sharpe, low-conviction directional bet; it earns its coupon with minimal duration drag regardless of macro outcome
1-year total return of 3.43% confirms the carry-dominant regime; upside beyond carry is negligible, downside capped by short duration — probability distribution is very tight around par

calls.name: iShares TIPS Bond ETF
drivers: 10y TIPS real yield near 2.1% (multi-year high) offers genuinely attractive real compensation; TIPS deliver positive real return even with CPI elevated — historically cheap vs nominal Treasuries
May headline CPI at 4.2% still exceeds the ~2.4% 10y breakeven, but the collapsing energy tail (Brent <$86) is pulling near-term breakevens lower, a modest headwind to principal accretion
Soft May core (+2.9% y/y) keeps underlying inflation sticky-but-easing; the stagflation-lite scenario remains TIPS' home turf over 12m
Duration risk (~6-7y) is still a headwind if real yields grind higher from elevated levels; recent auction demand was soft, limiting near-term momentum

calls.name: iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: OAS ~80bp is near historic tights vs 132bp long-run average — spread has almost no room to compress further, and mean-reversion risk of ~50bp widening would translate to ~4-5% price loss, partially offsetting a 5.24% SEC yield

Duration ~8-9y gives substantial rate sensitivity; if 10y yields push through 4.67% resistance on a hot CPI print, LQD faces combined spread-widening and rate losses — the asymmetry is unfavorable near-term
5.24% SEC yield is the most compelling argument for LQD: at ~130bp premium over the 10y Treasury (all-in carry), investors earn meaningful income even if spreads drift slightly wider over 12m

IG credit fundamentals remain solid (low default risk, solid corporate earnings), providing a floor; but institutional positioning is rich and the stagflation-lite regime historically precedes spread widening in late cycle

calls.name: iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: OAS ~262bp is near the long-term mean but well below recession-era wides (500-800bp); in a late-cycle stagflation-lite regime, HY spreads historically widen 50-150bp before default cycles peak — current spread is not a safety margin

Institutional put buying at historically high volumes (March 2026: 1.73M contracts, 95% puts) signals sophisticated money hedging HY credit risk aggressively — an unusual bearish signal from smart money

6.7% yield with ~4y duration provides meaningful carry, but a 100bp spread widening would generate roughly -4% price impact, fully consuming ~7 months of carry — downside skew is negative in stagflation tail

Default rate at 2.5% is currently benign but rising energy/financing costs in late-cycle environments typically push HY defaults toward 4-6% within 12-18m; forward default pricing leaves little cushion

calls.name: iShares J.P. Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond ETF
drivers: OAS ~170bp over Treasuries with an all-in yield ~6% (10y UST 4.47% + 153bp spread) offers reasonable carry pickup; in a carry-dominant regime where spread compression is unlikely, EMB investors earn their coupon with limited capital gain potential

USD strength near DXY 99 (OW call in macro framework) is a structural headwind for EM USD bonds via funding stress and capital flow reversal — a strong dollar historically drives EMB spreads wider by 20-50bp

Three macro triggers: (1) Fed hike extending higher-for-longer USD regime, (2) oil shock pressuring net-oil-importing EM sovereigns, (3) US fiscal/Moody's downgrade risk elevating risk-free rate globally — all three are live in current regime

Technical support: EM real yields exceed DM, EM inflation is falling in most countries unlike the US, and carry-seeking flows into EM debt funds provide a bid; net EM supply is low in 2026 reducing technical pressure

calls.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
drivers: Broad investment-grade exposure (~70% AAA/AA, mix of Treasuries, MBS, agencies, corporates) with ~6y duration means BND inherits moderate rate sensitivity — 10y yield near 4.56% caps upside near-term but 3.94% dividend yield provides ballast

Blended duration (~6y) sits in the 'belly' of the risk/reward curve — less punishing than TLT in a higher-for-longer scenario but more rewarding than SHY if yields eventually normalize; a reasonable all-weather allocation with better convexity than long-end peers

1y total return of only 0.61% reflects the drag from 2025's rate volatility; mean-reversion from depressed total returns historically improves 12m forward returns, and carry at ~4% annualized is additive from current price levels

MBS component (~20%) benefits from a no-recession base case (prepayment risk is contained, spreads are tight), while Treasury component provides a modest flight-to-quality hedge if the geopolitical tail materializes

calls.name: VanEck Rare Earth & Strategic Metals ETF
drivers: Live catalyst: China's MOFCOM blacklisted MP Materials, USA Rare Earth and ~8 other US firms on June 22 (retaliation for expanded US restrictions), tightening the Western supply picture and re-igniting the rare-earth re-rating theme
China controls ~70% of mining and ~90% of processing/magnets; every escalation of export curbs raises the strategic value of the ex-China basket REMX captures
But REMX holds a mix of Chinese and ex-China names, diluting the pure ex-China re-rating, and the basket is thin and highly volatile — a momentum vehicle, not a steady compounder
12m skew positive on structural Western on-shoring + DoD backing, but headline-driven and prone to sharp give-backs once a given escalation is priced

calls.name: MP Materials Corp
drivers: The marquee ex-China rare-earth name (Mountain Pass, CA) with the DoD as a stakeholder and $330M+ in prior defense contracts — Western government backing is a structural tailwind

China added MP to its export-control list June 22, but the curbs restrict what MP can RECEIVE from China, not its sales; net, China tightening ex-China supply raises MP's strategic pricing power and magnet-build economics
High operational leverage and a magnet-manufacturing ramp give outsized 12m upside if NdPr/dysprosium prices re-rate on the China squeeze
Risks: rich valuation prices in much of the strategic premium, execution on the downstream magnet build is unproven, and any US-China de-escalation would unwind the trade quickly

calls.name: USA Rare Earth Inc
drivers: Also blacklisted by China on June 22, underscoring its place in the Western critical-minerals supply chain (Round Top deposit + Stillwater magnet plant ambitions)
Earlier-stage and pre-cash-flow vs MP, so it is the higher-beta, more speculative expression of the on-shoring/DoD-backed magnet theme
China export curbs and US policy support (reshoring, defense demand) are the upside drivers; the stock re-rates hard on escalation headlines
Risks: execution, financing and dilution risk are acute for a pre-revenue developer; a de-escalation or capital raise would pressure the equity

calls.name: Lynas Rare Earths Ltd
drivers: The largest rare-earth producer outside China and the first non-China commercial producer of dysprosium oxide (Malaysia) — the cleanest ex-China supply story; Macquarie reiterated a bullish view as China's export squeeze tightens the market
US DoD-backed heavy-rare-earth processing (Texas) adds a Western-government revenue/strategic leg as China curbs raise ex-China value
Cash-generative and production-scaled, so less binary than the US developers — a relatively higher-quality way to own the theme
Risks: NdPr price sensitivity, Malaysian regulatory/operational overhang, and reversal risk if China relaxes curbs or prices soften

calls.name: Neo Performance Materials Inc
drivers: Owns the only operating rare-earth separation facility in Europe (Estonia) plus a new magnet plant — a downstream/processing play that benefits directly as the West races to build magnet capacity outside China
China's June 22 export-control escalation lifts the strategic value of ex-China processing and magnets, Neo's core franchise
More diversified (magnetics, chemicals, rare metals) than the single-asset miners, giving steadier cash flow but a more muted pure-theme beta
Risks: cyclical end-markets (autos, electronics), execution on the magnet ramp, and sensitivity to NdPr pricing and any China de-escalation

calls.name: Energy Fuels Inc
drivers: Dual critical-minerals exposure — a US uranium producer ALSO building rare-earth (NdPr) separation at White Mesa, Utah — so it rides both the nuclear/AI-power and the ex-China rare-earth themes
China's rare-earth curbs plus sub-$85/lb uranium that retains long-run AI-driven utility contracting demand give two independent 12m catalysts
Optionality and Western-supply strategic premium support a positive skew
Risks: high operational leverage, early-stage REE separation execution, and commodity-price (uranium + NdPr) sensitivity make it volatile and headline-driven

calls.name: JL MAG Rare-Earth Co (H)
drivers: The Chinese-incumbent counter-bet: JL MAG is a leading Chinese high-performance NdFeB magnet maker that benefits from China's dominant, protected position in processing/magnets

Double-edged: China's export curbs entrench domestic champions at home but can also crimp the overseas sales of Chinese magnet makers and invite Western substitution — a more two-sided setup than the ex-China names
Strong structural EV/wind/robotics magnet demand underpins the 12m volume story regardless of the trade fight
Risks: China-policy and export-control whiplash, HK-listing liquidity/sentiment, and the West's accelerating push to design Chinese magnets out of strategic supply chains
